models.title: Approximate geometric mean return from arithmetic mean and variance
models.summary: The owner approximates geometric mean return by subtracting half the sample variance from arithmetic mean return.

relationship.original_equation: Geometric mean return ≈ arithmetic mean return − sample return variance / 2
relationship.locator: Measures of Mean Return and Volatility of Returns
relationship.translation_notes: Returns are base-one dimensionless fractions; variance is squared fractional-return units. The divisor 2 is the approximation coefficient.

variables.definition: Mean-minus-half-variance approximation to the compound average simple return
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

assumptions: The returns are simple decimal returns over comparable equal-length periods, measured using a consistent series and reinvestment convention.
Variance uses the owner’s sample n−1 convention and squared decimal-return units; the sample has at least two observations.
The approximation is used in a small-return, moderate-dispersion regime and is not an exact identity.
limitations: The exact finite-sample second-order expansion uses the population-denominator variance of the realized sample, differing from n−1 sample variance by a factor of (n−1)/n.
The approximation can be inaccurate for volatile returns, short samples, or returns near −100%; the New Zealand Treasury discusses finite-horizon expected-return bias.
An approximate result below −100% is not a feasible geometric simple return when all gross returns are positive; compute the actual compounded return when available.
